Add Unified Neighborhood Edge Aggregation to a NICHESObject

Source: R/add_neighborhood_edge_agg.R
add_neighborhood_edge_agg.Rd

For each focal cell and each LRM pair, aggregates LR communication scores across all edges in the cell's neighborhood. Each neighborhood edge is classified into one of five mutually exclusive categories relative to the focal cell: out (focal cell sends), in (focal cell receives), cross (neither endpoint is the focal cell), self.autocrine (focal cell's own self-loop: SendingCell == ReceivingCell == focal cell), or other.autocrine (a neighbor cell's self-loop: SendingCell == ReceivingCell != focal cell).

Usage

add_neighborhood_edge_agg(
  niches.obj,
  n.cores = 1L,
  chunk.size = 50L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject with neighborhood slots populated.

n.cores

Positive integer. Retained for API compatibility; not used in the current sparse matrix implementation. Default 1L.

chunk.size

Positive integer. Number of LRM pairs processed per sparse matrix batch. Smaller values reduce peak memory at the cost of slightly more overhead; larger values are faster but require more RAM. Default 50L (about 12 batches for 558 LRMs). Reduce to between 20L and 30L on memory-constrained machines.

verbose

Logical. Emit progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

The input niches.obj with $aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg populated (always replaced).

Details

All three score methods (sum, mean, cmean) and the in/out ratio are always computed. The slot is always fully replaced on each call – there is no incremental update mode. This follows the same convention as Seurat slot-populating functions: call the function when you want a fresh result.

Results are stored as a sparse data.table keyed on (cell, LRM) at $aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg. Only (cell, LRM) pairs with at least one non-zero-score neighborhood edge are included.

Five-way edge classification

For a focal cell F and an edge (S -> R) in F's neighborhood:

self.autocrine

S == R == F. F's own self-loop edge. Checked first. count.self.autocrine is always 0 or 1 per (cell, LRM).

other.autocrine

S == R != F. A neighbor cell's self-loop edge; F is not the self-looping cell.

out

S == F and S != R. Focal cell is the sender.

in

R == F and S != R. Focal cell is the receiver.

cross

S != F and R != F and S != R. Edge between two neighbors; focal cell is not involved.

Columns produced

Count columns (always produced):

count.in, count.out, count.cross, count.self.autocrine, count.other.autocrine

Number of non-zero-score edges in each category for this LRM. Because $edge.data is sparse, every stored row represents an active edge. count.self.autocrine is always 0 or 1 per (cell, LRM).

count.total

Sum of all five category counts.

Score columns (all three methods always produced, for each category):

score.{cat}.sum

Total score across category edges.

score.{cat}.mean

Sum divided by total neighborhood edges ($neighborhood.meta$n.edges), including zero-score edges. LRM-agnostic denominator.

score.{cat}.cmean

Conditional mean: sum divided by the category count. NA when count is zero.

score.inout.ratio

score.in.sum / score.out.sum. NA when score.out.sum == 0.

See also

add_neighborhoods, add_neighborhood_composition, aggregate_NICHESObject

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_example)

obj <- add_neighborhood_edge_agg(NICHESv2_example, n.cores = 1L)
#> [add_neighborhood_edge_agg] Aggregating 80 cells x 15 LRMs x 1364 neighborhood edges (chunk.size = 50) ...
#>   [add_neighborhood_edge_agg] chunk 1 / 1 done.
#> [add_neighborhood_edge_agg] Done. 399 rows | 74 cells | 15 LRM pairs.
head(obj$aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg)
